items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear, but new batchInternal fields (commitDB, jobID, committedSeqNum, applyDuration, syncCompleted) and the durabilityTracker mu fields have no comments. Detecting the no-op via reflect Pointer comparison in isBatchDurableConfigured is opaque.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: durability.go is 625 lines, over the 500-line cap. The WAL-error handling block is copy-pasted in both commitWrite paths. The batch now holds a commitDB backref, so the tracker is coupled to Batch.SyncWait. The vfs/syncing_file.go change is unrelated.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: commitWrite flushable path: `if err != nil { if syncWG != nil {...} }` silently drops WAL write errors for non-sync batches, where the code used to panic. db.go manually drains `<-d.commit.logSyncQSem`. The Fatalf on commit error was removed.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: The new APIs are additive, but every non-sync commit now takes the tracker mutex (recordNonSyncCommit). prepare() was restructured so all sync commits use fsyncWait. Removing Fatalf changes behavior, and Batch.SeqNum() semantics changed for empty batches.
